texts.orig: Consider, as in [30], the knot 7 4 . This knot has 3 -genus 1 and hence C ( 7 4 ) ≤ 3 . Since 7 4 is hyperbolic, we have C ( 7 4 ) ≥ 2 . It therefore suffices to show that C ( K ) ≠ 2 . Now, suppose that C ( K ) = 2 . Since 7 4 has determinant 15, one can write out integral binary quadratic forms with determinant 15 (see e.g. Conway-Sloane [8]). Using a case analysis, it is then possible to show that no such binary quadratic form satisfies Theorem 4.1. Hence, it follows that C ( 7 4 ) = 3 = 2 ⋅ g ( 7 4 ) + 1 .

texts.orig: 4.3. Non-orientable slice genus. The (smooth) 4-genus of a knot K is the smallest genus among all surfaces properly embedded in B 4 such that ∂F = K . A well-known lower bound on the 4 -genus is ∣ σ ( K )∣/ 2 . In analogy with crosscap number, the (smooth) non-orientable slice genus γ ∗ ( K ) of a knot K in S 3 is defined as the smallest first Betti number of all compact connected non-orientable surfaces F smoothly embedded in B 4 such that ∂F = K . If K is slice, then γ ∗ ( K ) is defined to be 0 . In 1975, Viro [39] showed that γ ∗ ( 4 1 ) = 2 , and hence 4 1 does not bound a Möbius band in B 4 .

texts.orig: Another proof that γ ∗ ( 4 1 ) = 2 follows from a result of Yasuhara, which is proved using the Gordon-Litherland pairing. Recall that the quadratic form q ∶ H 1 ( F ; Z / 2 Z ) → Z / 2 Z of a knot K is defined by q ( x ) = x ⊺ Ax , where F is a Seifert surface of K and A is a Seifert matrix for F . The Arf invariant of K is the Arf invariant of this quadratic form. Hence, Arf ( K ) = 0 if q maps a majority of elements of H 1 ( F ; Z / 2 Z ) to 0 and otherwise Arf ( K ) = 1 . The Arf invariant is also the ( mod 2 ) coefficient of z 2 in the Conway polynomial of K . Note that there is a well-defined injection Z / 2 Z → Z / 8 Z given by x → 4 ⋅ x .
